candidate_relations.reason: Mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma is a B-cell neoplasm, whereas the reference is anaplastic large-cell lymphoma; the tumor is CD20-negative and strongly CD30-positive.
This is a wording variant of the reference diagnosis, anaplastic large-cell lymphoma.
Mediastinal gray zone lymphoma is distinct from anaplastic large-cell lymphoma and typically has overlapping Hodgkin and primary mediastinal B-cell features not established here.
Hodgkin lymphoma is distinct from anaplastic large-cell lymphoma; Reed–Sternberg-like cells are only a morphologic feature, and CD15 is negative.
Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma is incompatible with the reference ALCL and is not supported by the CD20-negative phenotype.
Lymphoma includes anaplastic large-cell lymphoma but omits the required specific subtype.
Anaplastic large-cell lymphoma is a non-Hodgkin lymphoma, but this label lacks the required ALCL subtype.
A mediastinal germ-cell tumor is not a lymphoma and does not match the nodal morphology or CD30-positive ALCL diagnosis.
Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma is distinct from ALCL and would characteristically show a B-cell phenotype rather than the reported profile.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different Hodgkin lymphoma subtype and lineage
